title: Exact-length certificate from an assignment
statement: Let $C,e\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a binary word, and let $a:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\\}$ agree with $x$ on every index $j<|x|$, using false as the default bit beyond the indexed word. Then there is a binary word $u$ of length $C(|x|+1)^e$ such that the first $|x|+C(|x|+1)^e$ bits assigned by $a$ form the concatenation $xu$.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ is a Boolean assignment on natural-number indices
For every $j<|x|$, $a(j)$ equals the $j$th bit of $x$
replaced: For all parameters $C$ and $e$, every instance $x$, and every assignment agreeing with $x$ on the first $|x|$ variables, there is a certificate $u$ of length exactly $C(|x|+1)^e$ such that the recovered input word of the first $|x| + C(|x|+1)^e$ variables is the concatenation of $x$ and $u$; the certificate polynomial is not enlarged and no bounded-length witness is substituted.
